claims.statement: For every finite ordinary tree T with independence counts i_j(T), first strict zero-extended descent x(T), and natural p satisfying x(T)+2<=p, 3p<2alpha(T)+1, and |V(T)|=2p+2, the complete sum over original leaves v with Delta_p(T-v)<0 of Delta_(p-1)(T-{v,s_v})-Delta_(p-1)(T-N_T[s_v]) is nonpositive.
claims.scope: Registered universal first-order-shell assertion; bounded exact search conducted only at p=7 and |V(T)|=16. All 19320 unlabeled ordinary trees at that order were generated; 1696 passed both rank guards.
claims.reason: The exact bounded census found no nonnegative complete sum among the 1696 eligible trees at p=7 and order 16 (maximum -906). This supports the assertion only at that finite rank and order; it neither proves nor refutes the universal shell claim.

limitations: The exhaustive computation covers only p=7 and order 16, not any other shell rank or order.
Finite census evidence is bounded computation and does not establish a universal inequality.
All claims remain proposed_worker_only; no authoritative status is awarded.
